mainTopic: Which כהנים get a share of the קדשים: the rule 'not fit, no share,' timing of purity, and the טבול יום debate
overview: This amud is about which כהנים get a share of the קדשים meat. It first finishes explaining why a כהן with a temporary מום gets a share right away. It then tests the משנה's rule, 'whoever is not fit gets no share.' After trying 'fit to eat,' the גמרא goes back to 'fit for the עבודה.' The answer is that the משנה only says who is left out, and the בעל מום is a special inclusion from a פסוק. Next, the משנה makes purity at זריקת דמים the deciding moment, which disagrees with אבא שאול. אבא שאול requires purity until הקטר חלבים, and רב אשי's question about becoming טמא in between ends in תיקו. רבא then retells רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's debate between a טבול יום and a pure כהן over a מנחה, a חטאת and the חזה ושוק. Each time the logic fails, but a פסוק shows that only the כהן who can serve gets to eat. רב אחאי asks why a בכור round is missing, and the גמרא explains that the בכור פסוק says 'yours,' so the proof would not have worked. Finally, the גמרא explains why this was taught in the bathroom: he could not help thinking about it.

steps.title: Why a temporary בעל מום still gets a share
steps.stepSummary: Finishing an earlier explanation: we might have thought that a כהן with a temporary מום is like a טמא and cannot eat until he is fixed, so the teaching is needed to show he does get a share.
steps.simpleTranslation: [One might have thought he is] like a טמא. Just as a טמא does not eat as long as he is not טהור, so too this one does not eat as long as he is not healed. That is why we are taught [that he does get a share].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer it began before this section. It is explaining why we needed a special teaching that a כהן with a temporary מום gets a share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A temporary מום will go away, just as טומאה goes away. So we might have compared the two and said: just as a טמא waits until he becomes טהור, the blemished כהן waits until he heals. The teaching blocks that comparison, so he eats and gets a share right away.

keyTerms.meaning: 'it teaches us': the extra lesson we needed

steps.whyThisMatters: It establishes that being blemished, even only for a while, does not stop a כהן from getting a share. This fact is used as a challenge in the very next lines.

phrases.english: [he is] like an impure one;
just as an impure one –
as long as he is not pure, he does not eat,
so too this one also –
as long as he is not healed, he does not eat;
[therefore] it teaches us [that he does get a share].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation from the previous section of why the teaching about a temporary מום was needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why a teaching is needed by showing the mistaken conclusion we would otherwise reach
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A כהן with a temporary מום is like a טמא and cannot eat until he heals.
steps.terutzMaskana: He receives a share and eats even before he heals.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה's general rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule: any כהן who is not fit does not get a share.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה said:] Anyone who is not fit, etc. [does not get a share of the meat].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה. This sets up the questions that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave a general rule that a כהן who is not fit does not get a share of the meat. The משנה does not say what 'fit' means. The next steps test that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: etc.: the rest of the quoted line

phrases.english: [The משנה said:] Anyone who is not fit, etc.
phrases.notes: The full line in the משנה ends 'does not get a share of the meat.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן who is not fit does not get a share in the קדשים.

steps.title: A blemished כהן is not fit for service, yet he gets a share
steps.stepSummary: Challenge: a בעל מום cannot do the עבודה, but the משנה itself says he gets a share.
steps.simpleTranslation: And doesn't [an unfit one get a share]? There is the בעל מום, who is not fit for the עבודה, and he does get a share!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule by reading 'not fit' as 'not fit for the עבודה.' The בעל מום breaks that rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemished כהן may not serve in the בית המקדש, so he is 'not fit.' Yet the משנה says he gets a share and eats. So 'not fit, no share' cannot be right as it stands.

keyTerms.meaning: a כהן with a physical blemish

phrases.english: And doesn't he?!
But there is a blemished one,
who is not fit for the service, yet he gets a share!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule 'anyone not fit does not get a share'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A counterexample: the בעל מום is unfit for עבודה, yet he gets a share.

steps.title: An impure כהן can serve communal offerings, yet gets no share
steps.stepSummary: A second challenge from the other side: a טמא may do the עבודה for קרבנות ציבור, yet he does not get a share.
steps.simpleTranslation: And further: this suggests that one who is fit for the עבודה gets a share. But there is the טמא with קרבנות ציבור, who is fit for the עבודה and does not get a share!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second attack. This time it reads the rule in reverse: if 'unfit' means no share, then 'fit' should mean a share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With קרבנות ציבור, a טמא כהן can serve, so he counts as fit for the עבודה. Yet he does not get a share. So the rule breaks in both directions: a fit כהן can get nothing, and an unfit כהן can get a share.

phrases.english: And furthermore, does that mean one fit for the service gets a share?!
But there is an impure one with communal offerings,
phrases.notes: Communal offerings can sometimes be brought even in טומאה, so this כהן is allowed to serve them.

phrases.english: who is fit for the service, and does not get a share!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge to the same rule, this time from the reverse direction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implied reverse of the rule: 'fit for עבודה means a share'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A counterexample: the טמא is fit to serve קרבנות ציבור, yet he gets no share.

steps.title: The משנה means fit for eating
steps.stepSummary: Answer: 'fit' in the משנה means fit to eat קדשים, not fit to serve.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה] is speaking about one who is fit for eating.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers both challenges at once by explaining what 'fit' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בעל מום may eat קדשים, so he gets a share. A טמא may not eat קדשים, so he does not. Both cases now fit the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: 'he is saying': this is what the text means

steps.whatToRemember: For now, the גמרא reads 'fit' as fit to eat. Step 8 will go back to the original reading, fit for the עבודה, so this is not the final answer.

phrases.english: It is saying 'fit for eating.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves both challenges in steps 3 and 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines a term in the משנה

steps.title: A minor may eat but gets no share
steps.stepSummary: Challenge to the new reading: a קטן may eat קדשים, yet he does not get a share.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is a קטן, who is fit for eating, and he does not get a share!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the new answer. If 'fit for eating' means a share, then the קטן breaks the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A young כהן is allowed to eat קדשים, but he does not get his own share. So 'fit to eat, therefore gets a share' seems to fail.

keyTerms.meaning: a minor (a child under bar מצוה)
but there is: introduces a counterexample

phrases.english: But there is a minor,
who is fit for eating, and does not get a share!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reverse of the new reading: 'fit to eat means a share'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A counterexample: the קטן may eat but gets no share.

steps.title: The משנה only teaches the negative side
steps.stepSummary: Answer: the משנה never said that anyone fit to eat gets a share. It only said that anyone unfit does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: This [the reverse rule] is not taught [in the משנה].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the קטן is no problem. The משנה only teaches 'unfit, no share.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being fit to eat is necessary for getting a share, but it is not enough by itself. A קטן can be fit to eat and still not get a share, and the משנה is not contradicted.

keyTerms.meaning: that is not what it teaches

steps.whatToRemember: Not fit to eat means no share. But being fit to eat does not automatically mean a share, as the קטן shows.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't flip the rule. 'Unfit means no share' does not mean 'fit means a share.' The משנה only says the first.

phrases.english: That it does not teach.
phrases.notes: He means the reverse rule, 'whoever is fit to eat gets a share,' is not in the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge from the קטן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the משנה's rule (no reverse inference)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה implies that whoever is fit to eat gets a share.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה only teaches that whoever is unfit to eat gets no share.

steps.title: Going back to the original reading of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: Now that we know the משנה only teaches what is unfit, the גמרא goes back to the first reading: 'fit' means fit for the עבודה. It answers both earlier questions.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have reached this point, you can really say it the way you first said it. If you ask about a טמא: the משנה does not teach that every fit כהן gets a share. If you ask about a בעל מום: the Torah included him on purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the idea from step 7 (the משנה only says who does NOT get a share) to return to its original reading. 'Unfit' here means unfit to do the עבודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The טמא question (step 4) goes away, because the משנה never said that every כהן fit to serve gets a share. The בעל מום question (step 3) goes away, because a פסוק specially includes him even though he cannot serve. So the first reading works after all.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that you have come to this (conclusion)
Really / actually (going back to an earlier position)
It (the משנה) does not teach this
The Torah included him (as a special case)

steps.whatToRemember: Final reading: a כהן who is unfit for the עבודה gets no share. A בעל מום is a special exception from a פסוק. The טמא is not a problem, because the משנה only lists who is excluded.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is throwing out step 7. It uses step 7's idea (the משנה only speaks about the unfit) to rescue the original meaning of 'fit'.

phrases.english: Now that you have come to this,
really it is as you said at the start;
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets, 'as he said'; the corrected wording in square brackets reads 'as you said'.

phrases.english: if you ask because of a טמא,
[the reverse rule, which would include] a טמא, is not taught,
and if you ask because of a בעל מום,
the Torah included him.
phrases.notes: This points back to the פסוק 'כל זכר' that the גמרא used earlier to include a בעל מום.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָתֵית לְהָכִי, לְעוֹלָם כִּדְקָאָמְרַתְּ מֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 7's point and uses it to bring back the original reading that steps 3 to 5 had pushed aside.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Return to the original reading, with a separate answer for each challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the original reading failed because of the טמא and the בעל מום.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Fit' means fit for the עבודה. The טמא is not addressed by the משנה, and the בעל מום is a special inclusion from the Torah.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whoever is unfit for the עבודה gets no share, except a בעל מום, whom the Torah includes.

steps.title: The משנה about purity at זריקה, and what follows from it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: a כהן who was טמא at זריקת דמים gets no share, even if he was pure at הקטר חלבים. It infers the reverse: pure at זריקה but טמא at הקטר, he does get a share.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: even if he was טמא when the blood was sprinkled and pure when the fats were burned, he does not get a share. So if he was pure when the blood was sprinkled, even if he was טמא when the fats were burned, he does get a share.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and draws out a precise inference from it. This sets up the next step, which will say who disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה makes the time of זריקת דמים the deciding moment. From this the גמרא learns that purity at הקטר חלבים does not matter at all. That inference is what conflicts with אבא שאול in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling of the blood on the מזבח
Burning of the fats on the מזבח
So then / this implies (introduces an inference)

phrases.english: Even if he was impure at the time of the sprinkling of the blood,
and pure at the time of the burning of the fats,
he does not get a share.
So if he was pure at the time of the sprinkling of the blood,
and impure at the time of the burning of the fats,
he gets a share;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: the next clause of the משנה, about timing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Purity at זריקת דמים decides whether he gets a share. Purity at הקטר חלבים does not matter.

steps.title: Our משנה does not follow אבא שאול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the משנה disagrees with אבא שאול. He requires the כהן to be pure from זריקה all the way until הקטר חלבים, based on a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה is not like אבא שאול. A ברייתא teaches that אבא שאול says: a כהן never eats unless he is pure from the time of sprinkling until the time the fats are burned. The פסוק says 'the one who offers the blood of the שלמים and the fat', so the fat-burning is also needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the inference from step 9 makes our משנה disagree with a known opinion, the view of אבא שאול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names both the blood and the fat. Because of that, אבא שאול holds that the כהן must be pure during both. Our משנה only looks at זריקה, so it cannot follow his view.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up two views: the משנה (only זריקה matters) and אבא שאול (purity is needed through הקטר). רב אשי's question in the next step works within אבא שאול's view.

phrases.english: Our משנה is not like אבא שאול.
As a ברייתא teaches: אבא שאול says:
He never eats,
phrases.notes: 'Eats' here means he gets a share of the meat.

phrases.english: unless he is pure from the time of sprinkling
until the time of the burning of the fats;
for the פסוק says:
'The one who offers the blood of the שלמים and the fat',
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:33

phrases.english: which shows that even the burning of the fats is also needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the inference in step 9 puts the משנה against אבא שאול's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to אבא שאול, a כהן gets a share only if he is pure from זריקה until הקטר חלבים, learned from the פסוק.

steps.title: רב אשי asks about becoming טמא in between
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks, within אבא שאול's view: what if the כהן was pure at זריקה and at הקטר, but became טמא in between?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי asked: if he became טמא in between, what is the law? Maybe we need him pure only at the time of sprinkling and at the time of burning, and here he was. Or maybe he must be pure the whole time, from the sprinkling until the burning of the fats?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי raises a question about how exactly to understand אבא שאול's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to read 'from זריקה until הקטר'. It could mean pure at both moments, so a break in the middle is fine. Or it could mean pure the whole time without any break. The case of becoming טמא in between and pure again is where the two readings give different answers.

phrases.english: רב אשי asked:
If he became impure in between, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He means he became טמא after the sprinkling and was pure again by the time the fats were burned.

phrases.english: Do we require purity at the time of sprinkling and at the time of burning,
and here he has that?
Or perhaps he must be pure

phrases.aramaic: מִשְּׁעַת זְרִיקָה וְעַד שְׁעַת הֶקְטֵר חֲלָבִים?
phrases.english: from the time of sprinkling until the time of the burning of the fats?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב אָשֵׁי: נִטְמָא בֵּינְתַיִים מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to understand the exact wording of אבא שאול's rule from step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether אבא שאול requires purity only at the two moments, or the whole time without a break.

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends רב אשי's question with תיקו: it stays unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא cannot answer רב אשי's question, so it leaves it open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source decides between the two readings of אבא שאול. So the case of a כהן who became טמא in between and pure again stays in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question remains unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: According to our משנה, only purity at זריקת דמים matters. According to אבא שאול, purity is needed through הקטר חלבים. Whether a break in the middle is allowed under his view is left as a תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes רב אשי's question from step 11 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Under אבא שאול's view, it remains in doubt whether becoming טמא in between takes away the כהן's share.

steps.title: רבא learned this rule from רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבא says he learned that a טבול יום gets no share from רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who set it up as a debate. A טבול יום asks for a share of a מנחה to eat at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: I learned this law from רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. He said: In the bathroom I argued it out. A טבול יום came and said, 'Give me some of a מנחה, and I will eat it later.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא names the source for the rule that a טבול יום gets no share. Then the story begins: a טבול יום asks for a share of a מנחה. This line sets up the debate that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טבול יום has already gone to the מקוה, but he is not fully pure until nightfall. He argues that by evening he could eat, so he should get his share now. The next steps show why he is turned down.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who went to the מקוה today but is not fully pure until nightfall

phrases.english: Rava said: This law
phrases.notes: This is the משנה's rule that a טבול יום gets no share of the קדשים.

phrases.english: I learned it from Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon,
who said: In the bathroom I argued it out –
A tevul yom came and said:
Give me from a meal offering and I will eat.
phrases.notes: He means he will eat it in the evening, once he is fully pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הַאי דִּינָא מֵרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן גְּמִירְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new rule in the משנה (טבול יום) and gives its source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rule that a טבול יום gets no share comes from רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, shown through a debate.

steps.title: The pure כהן's קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The pure כהן argues: I can already keep you from an Israelite's חטאת, where your rights are strong. So surely I can keep you from an Israelite's מנחה, where your rights are weak.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If, where your power is strong — with your own חטאת — I still push you away from an Israelite's חטאת, then where your power is weak — with your own מנחה — isn't it logical that I push you away from an Israelite's מנחה?
steps.whatsHappening: The pure כהן tries to prove with a קל וחומר that the טבול יום gets no share of a מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן eats from his own חטאת, so there he has 'strong power.' A כהן's own מנחה is never eaten, so there he has 'weak power.' If he loses out even on the strong one, he should surely lose out on the weak one.

keyTerms.meaning: Reasoning from a strong case to a weaker one

phrases.english: He said to him: Just as if
phrases.notes: The speaker now is the pure כהן handing out the shares.

phrases.english: in a place where your power is strong – with your sin offering,
I push you away from an Israelite's sin offering;
in a place where your power is weak – with your meal offering,
phrases.notes: A כהן's own מנחה is burned completely and never eaten.

phrases.english: is it not logical that I push you away from an Israelite's meal offering?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the טבול יום's request with a logical proof.
steps.raayaObject: A טבול יום gets no share of an Israelite's מנחה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from the חטאת, where his rights are stronger and he is still refused.

steps.title: The טבול יום breaks the קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The טבול יום answers: with a חטאת we are equal, both strong. With a מנחה we are also equal, both weak. So the comparison proves nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you push me away from an Israelite's חטאת, that is because there your power is strong just like mine. But will you push me away from an Israelite's מנחה, where your power is weak just like mine?
steps.whatsHappening: The טבול יום rejects the קל וחומר and shows it does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pure כהן said the טבול יום is 'weaker' with a מנחה. But the pure כהן is weak there too, since no כהן eats his own מנחה. Since both are equal in each case, there is no 'stronger vs weaker' to build a קל וחומר on.
steps.confusionAlert: Both speakers keep saying 'your power' and 'my power.' Here 'I/my' is the טבול יום and 'you/your' is the pure כהן.

phrases.english: But if you push me away from an Israelite's sin offering –
phrases.notes: Now the טבול יום is speaking.

phrases.english: that is because just as my power is strong
so too your power is strong;
will you push me away from an Israelite's meal offering,
phrases.notes: Some versions say just 'from a מנחה'; the square brackets give the corrected wording, 'from an Israelite's מנחה'.

phrases.english: where just as my power is weak
so too your power is weak!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר of step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole קל וחומר is thrown out.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The pure כהן is in the same position as the טבול יום in both cases, so there is no 'stronger' and 'weaker' case.

steps.title: The פסוק: only the one who offers it eats it
steps.stepSummary: The pure כהן drops logic and quotes a פסוק: the מנחה belongs to the כהן who offers it. Since a טבול יום cannot offer, he cannot eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'It shall belong to the כהן who offers it.' Come offer it, and then eat.
steps.whatsHappening: After the logic failed, the pure כהן proves his point from a פסוק. This ends the first round, about the מנחה. The טבול יום then moves on to the חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links eating to offering. A טבול יום may not do עבודה, so he cannot offer the מנחה. Therefore he gets no share of it, even though he could eat at night.
steps.whatToRemember: A טבול יום gets no share of a מנחה. The reason is not a קל וחומר (that failed) but the פסוק: only the כהן who can offer it gets to eat it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This links back to the earlier steps: having a share depends on being fit for the עבודה.

phrases.english: Behold, it says:
"It shall belong to the priest who offers it" –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:9

phrases.english: Come offer and eat.
phrases.notes: In other words: if you can't offer it, you can't eat it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר: לַכֹּהֵן הַמַּקְרִיב אֹתָהּ לוֹ תִהְיֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the קל וחומר is rejected, a פסוק settles the question.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A טבול יום gets no share of a מנחה because the פסוק gives it only to the כהן who can offer it.

steps.title: The טבול יום asks for a share of an Israelite's חטאת
steps.stepSummary: Having lost on the מנחה, the טבול יום now demands a share of an Israelite's חטאת, to eat in the evening.
steps.simpleTranslation: Give me a share of an Israelite's חטאת, and I will eat it.
steps.whatsHappening: The טבול יום makes a new claim, this time about a חטאת instead of a מנחה. This line sets up the second round of the debate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The structure repeats the earlier round, but the subject has changed. The טבול יום still cannot serve today, yet he wants meat he could eat tonight once he is fully pure.

keyTerms.meaning: A חטאת brought by a regular Jew (not a כהן)

phrases.english: Give me from the sin offering of an Israelite, and I will eat
phrases.notes: He means he will eat it tonight, after sunset, when he becomes fully pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the מנחה claim was settled by a פסוק, the טבול יום opens a parallel claim about a חטאת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The טבול יום claims a share of an Israelite's חטאת.

steps.title: The pure כהן argues with a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: If I can keep you from an Israelite's מנחה, where my own right is weak, then surely I can keep you from an Israelite's חטאת, where my own right is strong.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Where my power is weak, with my own מנחה, I already pushed you away from an Israelite's מנחה. So where my power is strong, with my own חטאת, isn't it logical that I push you away from an Israelite's חטאת?
steps.whatsHappening: The pure כהן tries to prove from logic that he can deny the טבול יום a share of the חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן's own מנחה gives him a weak position, and his own חטאת gives him a strong one. The argument goes from the weaker case to the stronger: if I win where I am weak (the מנחה), I should certainly win where I am strong (the חטאת).

keyTerms.meaning: I pushed you away (denied you a share)
Is it not logical? (the opening of a קל וחומר)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: וּמָה בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁהוֹרַע כֹּחִי –
phrases.english: He said to him: Just as in a place where my power is weakened,
phrases.notes: The speaker here is the pure כהן.

phrases.english: with my own meal offering, I pushed you away from an Israelite's meal offering;
a place where my power is strengthened, with my own sin offering,
is it not logical that I push you away from an Israelite's sin offering?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: וּמָה בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁהוֹרַע כֹּחִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the טבול יום's new claim with a logical proof.
steps.raayaObject: That a pure כהן can deny a טבול יום a share of an Israelite's חטאת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from the מנחה case, where the pure כהן's own right is weaker.

steps.title: The טבול יום shows the two cases are not comparable
steps.stepSummary: With the מנחה we are both weak, and with the חטאת we are both strong. So winning one does not prove you win the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You pushed me away from an Israelite's מנחה, where just as your power is weak, so is mine. Does that mean you can push me away from an Israelite's חטאת, where just as your power is strong, so is mine?!
steps.whatsHappening: The טבול יום rejects the קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if the other side stays the same while your side gets stronger. Here both sides get stronger together, because the טבול יום is also a כהן with his own חטאת. So the gap between them never changes, and the logic proves nothing.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: וּמָה אִם שֶׁדְּחִיתַנִי מִמִּנְחַת יִשְׂרָאֵל –
phrases.english: He said to him: But if you pushed me away from an Israelite's meal offering,
phrases.notes: Now the טבול יום is speaking.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכְּשֵׁם שֶׁהוֹרַע כֹּחֶךָ כָּךְ הוֹרַע כֹּחִי;
phrases.english: where just as your power is weakened, so too my power is weakened;
will you push me away from an Israelite's sin offering,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכְּשֵׁם שֶׁיִּפָּה כֹּחֶךָ כָּךְ יִפָּה כֹּחִי?!
phrases.english: where just as your power is strengthened, so too my power is strengthened?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: וּמָה אִם שֶׁדְּחִיתַנִי מִמִּנְחַת יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר of step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole קל וחומר from מנחה to חטאת.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both כהנים are equally weak in one case and equally strong in the other, so there is no real ‘weaker to stronger’ step.

steps.title: The פסוק settles it: only the כהן who serves may eat
steps.stepSummary: The pure כהן quotes the פסוק that the כהן who offers the חטאת eats it. A טבול יום cannot offer it, so he cannot eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: ‘The כהן who offers it as a חטאת shall eat it.’ Come offer it, and then eat.
steps.whatsHappening: After the logic fails, the pure כהן wins the argument with a פסוק, just as in the מנחה round.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The right to eat depends on being able to do the עבודה. A טבול יום may not serve today, so he loses his share of the meat, even though he could be pure by nighttime.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who offers the חטאת
Come offer it and then eat

steps.whatToRemember: In both rounds, logic could not settle the case, so a פסוק did: a כהן gets a share of a קרבן only if he is fit to offer it. A טבול יום is not, so he gets no share of the מנחה or the חטאת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ends the second round of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's debate. The third round, about the חזה ושוק of a שלמים, comes next.

phrases.english: The verse states:
“The priest who offers it as a sin offering shall eat it”
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:19

phrases.english: Come, offer it, and eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר: הַכֹּהֵן הַמְחַטֵּא אֹתָהּ יֹאכְלֶנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected logic of steps 18 and 19 with a פסוק.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Only a כהן fit to offer the חטאת may eat it, so a טבול יום gets no share.

steps.title: The טבול יום asks for the breast and thigh of a peace offering
steps.stepSummary: Having lost on the חטאת, the טבול יום now demands a share of the חזה ושוק of an Israelite's שלמים, to eat in the evening.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Give me some of the breast and thigh, and I will eat it.
steps.whatsHappening: The טבול יום makes a new demand, this time for the כהן's portion of a שלמים. This sets up the next round of the debate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the third offering he tries, after the מנחה and the חטאת. He again means he will eat in the evening, once he becomes fully pure.

keyTerms.meaning: The breast and thigh of a peace offering, the part given to the כֹּהֲנִים

phrases.english: He said to him: Give me
phrases.notes: The speaker is the טבול יום, making a new demand.

phrases.english: from the breast and thigh, and I will eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: תֵּן לִי מֵחָזֶה וָשׁוֹק וְאוֹכַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After losing on the חטאת, the טבול יום moves to a third offering type.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The טבול יום claims a share of the חזה ושוק of an Israelite's שלמים.

steps.title: A קל וחומר from the sin offering
steps.stepSummary: Your right to your own חטאת is strong, and I still kept you from an Israelite's חטאת. Your right to a שלמים is weak, since you only get the breast and thigh. So surely I can keep you from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Where your right is strong, with your own sin offering, I kept you from an Israelite's sin offering. Where your right is weak, with peace offerings, where you only get the breast and thigh, isn't it logical that I can keep you away?
steps.whatsHappening: The pure כהן argues with a קל וחומר. If he won where the טבול יום is strong, he should surely win where the טבול יום is weak.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן eats his own חטאת completely, so his right there is strong. With a שלמים he gets only the breast and thigh, so his right there is weak. Since the טבול יום already lost the חטאת in step 20, the pure כהן says he must lose the שלמים too.

keyTerms.meaning: I pushed you away, I kept you out
Isn't it logical? (opens a קַל וָחוֹמֶר)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: וּמָה בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁיִּפָּה כֹּחֲךָ –
phrases.english: He said to him: Just as in a place where your right is strong,
phrases.notes: Now the pure כהן is speaking.

phrases.english: with your own sin offering, I kept you away
from an Israelite's sin offering;
phrases.notes: Some versions say 'from the breast and thigh' in round brackets. The corrected wording in square brackets is 'from an Israelite's sin offering'.

phrases.english: then in a place where your right is weak, with peace offerings,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין לָךְ בָּהֶן אֶלָּא חָזֶה וָשׁוֹק,
phrases.english: where you get only the breast and thigh,
isn't it logical that I can keep you away?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: וּמָה בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁיִּפָּה כֹּחֲךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the demand in step 21 with a קל וחומר, built on the win over the חטאת in step 20.
steps.raayaObject: The טבול יום may not take the חזה ושוק of an Israelite's שלמים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from the חטאת, where the כהן's right is stronger and he was still kept out.

steps.title: Wives and slaves make the peace offering stronger
steps.stepSummary: The טבול יום answers that in one way his right to the חטאת is weaker: his wives and slaves cannot eat it, but they can eat the חזה ושוק. So the קל וחומר falls apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you kept me from the sin offering, where my right is weak because my wives and slaves cannot eat it, does that mean you can keep me from the breast and thigh, where my right is strong because my wives and slaves can eat it?!
steps.whatsHappening: The טבול יום breaks the קל וחומר. He shows that the חטאת is not stronger in every way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת may be eaten only by male כהנים, while the חזה ושוק may be eaten by a כהן's whole household. So in that respect the שלמים is the stronger right. Each offering is strong in a different way, so winning on one does not prove a win on the other.

keyTerms.meaning: My wives and my slaves (the כֹּהֵן's household)
If it is true that... (opens a pushback)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two kinds of 'strength.' The pure כהן measured how much of the animal the כהן gets. The טבול יום measures who in his household may eat it.

phrases.english: If you kept me away from a sin offering,
phrases.notes: The טבול יום is answering back.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן הוֹרַע כֹּחִי אֵצֶל נָשַׁיי וַעֲבָדַיי;
phrases.english: where my right is weak when it comes to my wives and my slaves;
phrases.notes: Only male כהנים may eat a חטאת, so his household cannot share it.

phrases.english: will you keep me away from the breast and thigh,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן יִפָּה כֹּחִי אֵצֶל נָשַׁיי וַעֲבָדַי?!
phrases.english: where my right is strong when it comes to my wives and my slaves?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר of step 22.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole קל וחומר from חטאת to שלמים.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The חטאת is not stronger in every way. In who may eat it (wives and slaves), the שלמים is stronger.

steps.title: The verse: the one who sprinkles the blood eats
steps.stepSummary: The pure כהן quotes the פסוק that the שלמים belong to the כהן who sprinkles its blood. A טבול יום cannot sprinkle, so he cannot eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'It shall be the priest's who sprinkles the blood of the peace offerings.' Come sprinkle and eat!
steps.whatsHappening: As with the מנחה and the חטאת, the pure כהן stops using logic and ends the argument with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק ties eating the שלמים to doing the עבודה of sprinkling the blood. A טבול יום may not do עבודה, so he has no share. 'Come sprinkle and eat' is a challenge: you can't, so you can't eat.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who sprinkles (the blood on the מִזְבֵּחַ)

steps.whatToRemember: Every round ends the same way. Logic could not settle the מנחה, the חטאת or the שלמים, but a פסוק did each time: only a כהן who can do the עבודה gets to eat. A טבול יום cannot do עבודה, so he gets no share.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the rule that a כהן's share in an offering depends on being able to serve in it at that time.

phrases.english: The verse says:
"To the priest who sprinkles the blood of the peace offerings
it shall belong" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא ז:יד

phrases.english: come sprinkle, and eat!
phrases.notes: He is saying: you can't sprinkle today, so you can't eat either.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר: לַכֹּהֵן הַזּוֹרֵק אֶת דַּם הַשְּׁלָמִים לוֹ יִהְיֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the קל וחומר was rejected in step 23, the pure כהן settles the question with a פסוק.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A טבול יום gets no share of an Israelite's שלמים, because only the כהן who sprinkles the blood may eat, and he cannot sprinkle.

steps.title: The story ends: the טבול יום leaves with nothing
steps.stepSummary: The טבול יום walks out with all his clever arguments wasted. An אונן walks on his right and a מחוסר כפרה on his left, and none of them gets a share.
steps.simpleTranslation: The טבול יום left with his קל וחומר arguments on his head. An אונן walked on his right, and a מחוסר כפרה walked on his left.
steps.whatsHappening: The story closes with a picture: the טבול יום leaves without any share, and two other כהנים who cannot do the עבודה leave with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All of the טבול יום's arguments failed, because each time the pure כהן found a פסוק that ties eating to doing the עבודה. The אונן and the מחוסר כפרה cannot do the עבודה either, so the same rule leaves them without a share too.

keyTerms.meaning: A mourner on the first day, before the burial of a close relative
Someone who still has to bring a קרבן to finish becoming pure

steps.whatToRemember: A כהן who cannot do the עבודה that day (a טבול יום, an אונן, a מחוסר כפרה) does not get a share in the קרבנות, even to eat later.

phrases.english: The טבול יום went out
with his kal vachomer arguments on his head,
phrases.notes: Literally 'his light and heavy things.' He means all his קל וחומר arguments came back on him and got him nothing.

phrases.english: an onen on his right,
and a mechusar kapparah on his left.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָצָא טְבוּל יוֹם קוּלָּיו וַחֲמוּרָיו עַל רֹאשׁוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story after the pure כהן's final פסוק about the שלמים in Step 24.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The טבול יום, together with the אונן and the מחוסר כפרה, gets no share of the קרבנות.

steps.title: רב אחאי asks: why not request a share of a בכור?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחאי points out that the טבול יום had one more request he could have made: a share of a בכור, to eat in the evening.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחאי challenges: Let the טבול יום say to him, 'Give me some of a בכור and I will eat.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחאי questions the story. Why didn't the טבול יום also ask for a share of a בכור?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story listed the טבול יום's attempts with the מנחה, the חטאת and the שלמים, but it never mentioned the בכור. רב אחאי is asking why this obvious extra claim is missing, and this sets up the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenges, he raises a difficulty
A firstborn animal, which is given to a כהן

phrases.english: Rav Achai challenges:
Let him say to him:
phrases.notes: The טבול יום speaking to the pure כהן.

phrases.english: Give me some of a firstborn, and I will eat!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks back at the finished story and points to a request the טבול יום never made.
steps.kashyaTarget: The story's list of the טבול יום's claims
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The טבול יום asked for a share of a שלמים to eat in the evening. He could just as well have asked for a share of a בכור, so why doesn't the story mention it?

steps.title: A possible answer: a קל וחומר blocks the בכור
steps.stepSummary: Maybe he didn't ask because the pure כהן would answer with a קל וחומר. I could keep you from the חטאת, where my rights are weaker. So I can surely keep you from the בכור, which belongs to me completely.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the pure כהן could say to him: In the חטאת, my rights are weaker, since my wives and slaves cannot eat it, and still I kept you away from an Israelite's חטאת. In the בכור, my rights are stronger, since all of it is mine. Isn't it logical that I can keep you away from it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests an answer to רב אחאי. The טבול יום didn't ask for a בכור because the pure כהן had a קל וחומר ready to block it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only male כהנים may eat a חטאת. A בכור, though, is given fully to one כהן, and his whole household may eat it. If the pure כהן can push the טבול יום away even where his own rights are weaker, then surely he can do so where his rights are stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: I pushed you away, I kept you out

steps.confusionAlert: In Step 23 it was the טבול יום who used the 'wives and slaves' point. Here the pure כהן uses that same point to argue for himself.

phrases.english: Because he could say to him:
phrases.notes: Now it is the pure כהן speaking to the טבול יום.

phrases.english: If where my rights are weaker
in a sin offering, as far as my wives and slaves go,
phrases.notes: Only male כהנים eat a חטאת, so his wives and slaves get none of it.

phrases.english: I pushed you away from an Israelite's sin offering;
then where my rights are stronger, in a firstborn,
since all of it is mine,
isn't it logical that I can push you away from it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an answer to רב אחאי's question in Step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: קל וחומר that the pure כהן could use to block the claim
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The טבול יום should have asked for a share of a בכור.
steps.terutzMaskana: He didn't ask, because the pure כהן could block him with a קל וחומר from the חטאת.

steps.title: The טבול יום could break that קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The טבול יום could answer: in a חטאת, both of us have weaker rights. In a בכור, both of us have stronger rights. So you cannot learn the בכור from the חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you kept me from a חטאת, where your rights are weaker and so are mine, will you keep me from a בכור, where your rights are stronger and so are mine?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the answer in Step 27 does not work. The טבול יום could knock down the pure כהן's קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whatever makes the pure כהן's rights stronger in a בכור makes the טבול יום's rights stronger in the same way, because his household could eat it too. Both of them gain equally, so the pure כהן has no extra edge to build a קל וחומר on, and רב אחאי's question comes back.

phrases.english: But if you pushed me away from a sin offering,
phrases.notes: Now the טבול יום is answering back.

phrases.english: where just as your rights are weaker,
so too my rights are weaker;
will you push me away from a firstborn,
where just as your rights are stronger,
so too my rights are stronger?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר that Step 27 offered as the answer to רב אחאי.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The קל וחומר from the חטאת to the בכור
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The stronger rights in a בכור belong to both כהנים equally, so the pure כהן has no special advantage to build the קל וחומר on.

steps.title: The pure כהן could quote a verse about the firstborn
steps.stepSummary: A second try at answering רב אחאי. The pure כהן could have quoted a פסוק about the בכור: 'their meat shall be yours,' which seems to mean come sprinkle the blood and then eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'You shall sprinkle their blood on the altar and burn their fat... and their meat shall be yours.' So come sprinkle and eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The קל וחומר was knocked down in step 28. So the גמרא tries another way the pure כהן could have kept the טבול יום away from the בכור: by quoting a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק about the בכור, the words 'their meat shall be yours' come right after sprinkling the blood. The pure כהן reads this as tying the eating to the sprinkling. A טבול יום cannot sprinkle, so he would not get to eat.

keyTerms.meaning: Come sprinkle and eat: only the one who sprinkles eats

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר: ״אֶת דָּמָם תִּזְרֹק עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ
phrases.english: The verse says: 'You shall sprinkle their blood on the altar
phrases.notes: במדבר 18:17–18, about the בכור.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶת חֶלְבָּם תַּקְטִיר... וּבְשָׂרָם יִהְיֶה לְךָ״
phrases.english: and you shall burn their fat... and their meat shall be yours'
So come sprinkle and eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the קל וחומר failed in step 28, a פסוק is offered instead to answer רב אחאי's question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Scriptural source instead of logical argument
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The טבול יום should have asked for a share of the בכור.
steps.terutzMaskana: The pure כהן could block him with the פסוק, which links eating to sprinkling.

steps.title: The verse says 'yours', meaning even another כהן
steps.stepSummary: The טבול יום refutes the reading. The פסוק never says 'to the כהן who sprinkles.' It says 'yours,' meaning the meat can go to any כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The other one (the טבול יום) would refute this: Does it say 'their meat goes to the כהן who sprinkles'?! It says 'their meat shall be yours,' even to a different כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The טבול יום knocks down the pure כהן's פסוק. The wording of the בכור verse does not limit the meat to the one who sprinkled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the מנחה, the חטאת and the שלמים, the פסוק says the meat belongs to the כהן who offers it or sprinkles its blood. For the בכור, it only says 'yours', which can mean any כהן. So this פסוק would not have won the argument, and that is why the story leaves out a בכור round. It is not a ruling that a טבול יום gets a share of a בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (here, the טבול יום)
Is it written...?! (meaning: it is not written)
A different כהן, not the one who did the service

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 24. There the שלמים verse really does say the meat belongs to the כהן who sprinkles. The בכור verse does not say that, and that is the whole point here.

phrases.english: And the other one would refute:
phrases.notes: 'The other one' is the טבול יום.

phrases.english: Is it written 'and their meat goes to the כהן who sprinkles'?!
What is written is 'and their meat shall be yours'
which means even to a different כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the פסוק offered in step 29.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the reading of the בכור verse as limiting the meat to the sprinkler.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The verse says 'yours', not 'to the כהן who sprinkles', so it includes any כהן.

steps.title: How could he teach Torah in the bathroom?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to where the story was told. It asks how רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון could teach this in the bathroom, since רבי יוחנן says thinking Torah is forbidden in a bathhouse or bathroom.
steps.simpleTranslation: How could he do this? But didn't רבה בר בר חנה say in the name of רבי יוחנן: In every place it is permitted to think about Torah, except the bathhouse and the bathroom!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the debate between the כהנים. It now questions the setting of the story, since it was taught in the bathroom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבא said this teaching was given in the bathroom. That seems to break רבי יוחנן's rule against even thinking Torah there. So the גמרא challenges how a great sage could do this.

keyTerms.meaning: And how could he do this?

phrases.english: And how could he do this?
phrases.notes: He means רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who taught this in the bathroom, as רבא said earlier.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: But didn't רבה בר בר חנה say in the name of רבי יוחנן:
In every place it is permitted to think about Torah,
except the bathhouse and the bathroom!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the content of the story to the setting where it was taught.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון teaching Torah in the bathroom.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן forbids even thinking Torah in a bathroom, so teaching it there seems forbidden.

steps.title: When he can't help it, it is different
steps.stepSummary: The answer: he did not choose to do it. The thought took over his mind and he could not help it, and that case is different.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it happens because he can't help it, it is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. רבי יוחנן's rule is about choosing to think Torah, and this was not something he chose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון was so caught up in the question that it came out of him on its own. Something forced on a person is not counted the same as something he chooses. So רבי יוחנן's rule still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Something forced, that a person can't help

steps.whatToRemember: The story leaves out a בכור round because neither the קל וחומר nor the פסוק would have worked there: the בכור verse says 'yours', not 'to the כהן who sprinkles'. The story was taught in the bathroom only because he could not help thinking about it.

phrases.english: When he can't help it, it is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 31.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He broke רבי יוחנן's rule by teaching Torah in the bathroom.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule covers choosing to think Torah. Something a person cannot help is different.
